survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIAAC) and therefore does not implement sampling weights, replicate weights, or PV-based scaling. The document describes governance structures, institutional responsibilities, and expenditure shares for Luxembourg’s adult skills system across national and local levels. Because there is no assessment administration, no achievement scaling, and no student-level outcome modeling, weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) are not applicable. The appropriate “data preparation” here is conceptual compilation from available sources rather than statistical preprocessing of survey responses.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a governance and institutional mapping note, not an empirical analysis of cognitive achievement or other PV-based outcomes. As a result, plausible values (PV) are not generated or used, and there is no missing-data handling step for student responses. The note synthesizes publicly available information on responsibilities and funding allocation rather than estimating model parameters from an assessment dataset.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Not applicable: the note does not define an analytic student sample; it compiles governance information for Luxembourg’s adult skills system from available sources.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Luxembourg country note provides a descriptive overview of how the adult skills system is governed, focusing on the allocation of responsibilities across strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, and delivery. It characterises Luxembourg as highly centralised, with adult education and training (VET, CET, and AE) overseen nationally by the Ministry of Education, Children and Youth, supported by national agencies and social partners. It also details the roles of the Ministry of Higher Education and Research (HVET), the Ministry of Labour (ALMP design via ADEM), and expert councils/committees that advise on labour-market and skills needs. At the local level, municipalities (100 communes) have limited formal oversight but contribute through non-formal adult learning opportunities and integration-oriented courses. No assessment instruments, sampling frames, scaling procedures, or PV-based benchmarks are used because the note is not an empirical student-outcome study.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the document is a non-empirical governance country note rather than an ILSA-based empirical study. It contains no student-level dataset, no model training or predictive targets, and no reported sample sizes or performance metrics. Therefore, fields related to PV handling, missing-data procedures, ML techniques, and structured predictive findings are intentionally left empty or set to non-applicable categories.
